elements.title: TOTAL EXTERNAL DEBT STOCK, 2025
elements.description: The headline indicator shows total external debt stock of US$335.0 million in 2025, up 12.9% from 2024.

elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: Total external debt generally rises between 2015 and 2025, with an initial dip and a smaller dip near the end of the period. The printed endpoint values are US$116.7 million in 2015 and US$335.0 million in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 2
elements.title: External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations

data.label: Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type
Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type
Public & publicly guaranteed - by creditor type

elements.description: The top bar divides total external debt into public and publicly guaranteed and short-term debt. A connecting band leads to a bar dividing public and publicly guaranteed debt into multilateral and bilateral creditors, which then leads to separate creditor breakdowns. Asian Dev. Bank is the largest named creditor at US$188.7 million; Japan accounts for all US$22.0 million of bilateral debt.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show external debt and debt service relative to exports and GNI from 2015 to 2025, alongside shaded percentile bands. The printed 2025 ratios range from 39% for external debt / exports to 1% for debt service / GNI.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes present maturity, grace period and interest rate for official and private creditors. The official-creditor box shows 40 years, 10 years and 1.0%, respectively; the private-creditor box shows '..' for all three terms.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
